Faculty Senate Meeting
Faculty Senate meetings are scheduled monthly from 3-5pm during the academic year. Sponsored receptions typically follow the meetings. These are great opportunities to build collegial relationships and network with colleagues from other disciplines. Special Meetings may be called upon due notice.
Meetings will be held in person at a pre-determined location on the Kinston Campus, as well as remotely on Zoom. Please check back to this page for up-to-date meeting locations and Zoom links. In September, December, and April, the General Faculty-Graduate Faculty Meeting directly precedes the Faculty Senate Meeting.
For more information, including zoom links and current and past Senate agendas, visit the Faculty Senate Meeting website.

New Course Proposal Walkthrough
New Course Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Course Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Navigate by Section
Related toolkit entry: Specialization Modification Proposal Walkthrough

Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
How the Curriculum Process Works
Related toolkit entry: How the Curriculum Process Works
Approval Calendar

You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
Kuali Basics
Related toolkit entry: Kuali Basics

Some course proposal types can be easily confused. If you are unsure which type applies, review these common examples.
Table columns: If you want to… | Use…
If you want to…: Make a Temporary Course a Permanent Course which appears in the Academic Catalog | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new cross-listing to accompany an existing course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Add a new topic to an open-ended topics course | Use…: New Course Proposal if the course is a GCH course No proposal needed for any other subject code. Contact Enrollment Services to add the new topic.
If you want to…: Add a new topic to a permanent topics course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new 500-level section of a course to accompany the 400-level | Use…: New Course Proposal

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Courses.
On the Courses page, select + New Course in the upper-right corner.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the course to become effective. If the effective term entered at proposal submission has missed the deadline by the time it reaches the Faculty Senate, this field will be automatically updated to the next available semester.
Academic Career Select the appropriate Academic Career from the available options. You may only choose one option. If you plan to offer this course in both the traditional and accelerated calendars, please provide a rationale in the Supporting Materials file upload gadget that comes after the description.
College Select the college in which the course is housed.
Department Select the department in which the course is housed.
Honors Program Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Honors Program.
Honors Type Select HPR Course or H-section of Existing Course.
General Education Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “No” is chosen for General Education.
Temporary Course Select Yes or No.

Subject Code The subject code must be owned by the College and Department previously entered in the form.
Number A validation error will occur if you use a number already in use by the subject code. The course numbering system is found in UM 8.30.10.
Temporary course numbers end with an “X”
Grand Challenge course numbers end with a “G”
Is this a 400-level course available for graduate credit? Required for all courses. Select Yes or No, regardless of the course level.
Course Title
Abbreviated Course Title 29-characters max.
Course Description Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
URI course descriptions include additional course information such as credits, cross-listed courses, method of instruction, class hours, requisites, grading, graduate credit, and general education outcomes. Descriptions will be formatted to the catalog standard prior to final approval.
Supporting Materials Optional. Use this file upload to provide additional information that may be helpful to review committees before the proposal enters the approval workflow.

Modality Select all applicable options to indicate whether the course will be offered in person, online, or both. The specific modalities are provided for reference next to the checkboxes and are also defined in University Manual 8.30.30
Method of Instruction All courses must have at least one method of instruction. Note that “Online” is not a method of instruction; it was removed from the list of methods of instruction in 2025.
If the course has multiple methods of instruction, select the first as Primary and all additional methods as Secondary.
If the course has two or more methods of instruction, indicate how the methods are divided. This information is important for Enrollment Services; omitting it may delay final approval.
Requisites Can include prerequisites, corequisites, antirequisites, or other enrollment requirements.

Is this a cross-listed course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this a cross-listed course?
Cross-listed course(s) for eCampus Click “Add New” to add all cross-listings.
Cross-listed course(s) for the Catalog Click the “+” and add all cross-listings again.
Cross-listed Department(s) Add all departments belonging to the cross-listed courses, even if one or more belong to the same department.
Letter(s) of support from cross-listed departments For new courses and course modifications, the “parent” department (the department associated with the course code on the proposal) must provide a letter of support from each cross-listed department.
What if my cross-listed course code belongs to the same department as the parent course code? For example, MCE and ISE are both in the Department of Mechanical, Industrial & Systems Engineering.
Just upload a document stating: “Both subject codes belong to the same department.”

Credits First, select whether the course has fixed credits or a credit range. Then enter the applicable credit amount(s) in the fields provided.
Grading Method Select letter grades, S/U, or both.
Can this course be repeated for credit? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can this course be repeated for credit?
Maximum times course may be taken: Enter max number of times.
Maximum credits allowed: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn for the course. For example, a 3-credit course that may be taken three times for credit has a maximum of 9 credits.
Can students repeat within the same term? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can students repeat within the same term?
Maximum credits allowed per term: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn from this course within a single term.

Explain the purpose of the course. Enter a brief explanation of the course's purpose.
How is this course used within the curriculum? Select the appropriate option from the provided radio buttons.
🔽 The following field will appear only if if Core requirement… is chosen from How is this course used within the curriculum?
List all degree, major, minor, and certificate programs for which this course is required. List the name of all applicable programs for which the course is a required component.
By checking this box, I acknowledge that all courses must be approved via Faculty Senate vote before a program can be reviewed for final approval. Check the box to acknowledge that the course must receive Faculty Senate approval before a program requiring the course can receive final approval.
Content Overlap: Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units that may have related or overlapping curricular interests? Select Yes or Not Applicable.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen from Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units…?
Supporting Documentation Provide documentation demonstrating consultation with departments that have related or potentially overlapping curricular interests.

This section is completed by the Department Chair or, when applicable, the Director, Area Coordinator, or College Curriculum Committee Chair. Proposers should leave this section blank and proceed to the next section.
For those responsible for completing this section:
Certification by the Department Chair, Director, or Area Coordinator responsible for administering the course. Check the box to certify that the proposal has received the required approval by the faculty of the originating academic unit.
Name of Department Chairperson, Director, or Area Coordinator Enter your name.
Date of Faculty Vote Enter the date the faculty voted on the proposal.

🔽 This section will appear only if Yes is chosen from General Education.
Learning Outcome 1 Select the appropriate learning outcome from the dropdown and complete the table for your first outcome.
Learning Outcome 2 Courses must have at least one General Education learning outcome and may have up to two. Based on your selection for Learning Outcome 1, the applicable options will be available in this dropdown. If you are not adding a second outcome, leave this field blank.
If selected, complete the table for your second outcome.
Is this a grand challenge? Select Yes or No.

🔽 This section will appear only if the course is for general education credit, and if Yes is chosen for Is this a grand challenge?
To qualify for the grand challenge overlay, complete the following questions.
GRAND CHALLENGE: Explain how the course title, syllabus, and assignments demonstrate the contemporary challenge addressed by the course.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Explain how the course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and provides opportunities for students to make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Provide an abbreviated reading list organized by discipline that demonstrates the course’s disciplinary perspectives, and explain how each disciplinary perspective is integrated into major course assignments and activities.
ETHICS: Identify the ethical framework that allows students to weigh/evaluate issues. This topic needs to show up explicitly in the course schedule.
ETHICS: List the readings pertaining to ethics.
ETHICS: Describe how ethics is incorporated in some/all of the assignments and activities.

Once the proposal is submitted to the workflow, it is automatically routed to the Library Subject Selector, who will complete and upload the Library Impact Statement. Other than completing the prompts in this section, no additional action is required from the proposer.
Supplementary resources you expect to use in proposed course Select all that apply.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Other is chosen from Supplementary resources...
If Other, please specify:
Will students conduct library research in this course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if YES is chosen from Will students conduct library research...?
Please describe assignment(s) in detail.
LIST the critical journals, monographs, and electronic resources in the field that the University Library MUST have in order to support this course or program:
LIST any additional journals, monographs and electronic resources in the field that would support the course, but are NOT essential:
Library Impact Statement Document The Library Subject Selector will upload this to the proposal after the proposer submits to the workflow.

Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
Date: September 30, 2026 (2026-09-30)
Tags: Temp Course Email
New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.
